companyRankingLists.itemDescription: HP Inc., a global provider of computers and printing products, believes that diversity, equity, and inclusion are a business imperative, and has set specific goals related to gender and race in leadership and to closing the digital divide. The company’s Racial Equality and Social Justice Task Force identifies opportunities to reinforce equality in the company by hiring more people of color and minorities, influencing the industry, and advocating for equal opportunities through public policy and civil action. This past year, the company has advocated for federal funding for historically Black colleges and universities, and supported national recognition of and state-level protections for LGBTQ+ marriages. It also offers health care programs, like Black Health, which aims to ensure culturally competent health care and improved health outcomes for Black employees; and LGBTQ+ Health, to help queer-identifying people secure specialized care providers who understand community-specific risks. In 2023, HP created a “Beyond the Spectrum” toolkit to support families and caregivers of people with Autism Spectrum Disorder, offering advice on therapy, complexities of care, and emotional support.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription:
Equity was the focus for this personal computing and device titan in the past year, leading one employee to call it “an extremely ethical company at its very core” and noting that it “represents that aspect throughout every business unit.”

  • Volunteer communities of HP employees, called Business Impact Networks (BINs), are key to attracting and retaining diverse talent. This year, HP launched the Standing Ovation Awards to acknowledge the contributions of the different BINs.

  • The “Hire EQ: Equitable hiring for better outcomes” training program teaches managers to create a more diverse pipeline and create a better experience for all employees to grow.

  • Now in its third year, the Racial Equality and Social Justice Task Force works to identify, execute on, and hold the company accountable to the biggest opportunities it has to drive sustainable impact in racial equality.

  • When it comes to starting a family, the benefits offered to heterosexual couples are no different than same-sex couples, including equal paid leave policies.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: In 2022, HP was the only tech company to receive A ratings from the Carbon Disclosure Project for its sustainability efforts, including reaching zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2040 and counteracting deforestation for non-HP paper products used in its printers by 2030. HP jumped from No. 9 in the 2022 Modern Board 25 ranking to seven this year. Outgoing Levi Strauss CEO Chip Bergh has helmed HP’s board since 2017, bringing experience in consumer goods as the tech company doubles down on consumer electronics since its 2015 decoupling from Hewlett Packard’s enterprise tech business. Notable board members include Bruce Broussard, CEO of health care company Humana; Stacy Brown-Philpot, former CEO of TaskRabbit; and Judith Miscik, CEO of geopolitical consulting firm Kissinger Associates and former CIA deputy director of intelligence. After a 2022 net revenue drop of 0.8% year over year, the company announced a cost-cutting plan to save $1.4 billion through 2025, including 6,000 employee layoffs over the next three years. Forty-six percent of HP’s 13-person board (12 of whom are independent) are members of underrepresented groups, and 46% are women.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription:
Slowing computer sales hit HP, the computer and printer maker, in 2022 as its net revenue dropped 0.8% to $63 billion in 2022 and it announced job cuts.

  • As the PC slump dragged on, HP acquired audio conferencing and headset company Poly in August 2022.

  • In late 2022 HP announced plans to lay off almost 10% of its workforce over the next three years as it aims to shave $1.4 billion in costs by the end of the 2025 fiscal year.

  • HP reported in February 2023 that net revenue for its personal systems unit, made up largely of PCs, was down 24% from a year earlier.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription:
HP focuses on consumer technology, in contrast to fellow Hewlett-Packard corporate scion Hewlett Packard Enterprise, No. 2 on this list, which focuses on enterprise tech. HP scored a major coup in April 2022 when Warren Buffett’s holding company, Berkshire Hathaway, disclosed a $4.2 billion, 11% stake in the company—a vote of confidence in its long-term strategy that caused its stock price to soar.

HP’s board scored well for gender equality, age dispersion, and board independence. Chip Bergh, the CEO of Levi Strauss, has been the board chair at HP since 2017. Board member Bruce Broussard is CEO of Humana and former chief of McKesson Specialty/US Oncology.

Other former CEOs on the board include Shumeet Banerji (Booz & Company) and Robert R. Bennett (Discovery and Liberty Media). Stephanie A. Burns is the former CEO of Dow Corning and also sits on the board of Corning, as well as food manufacturer Kellogg.

Stacy Brown-Philpot is the former CEO of TaskRabbit and was previously entrepreneur-in-residence at Google, in addition to holding multiple leadership roles at the tech giant. She’s also on the investment committee of the SB Opportunity Fund, a venture fund for Black, Latinx, and Native American founders.

Aída Álvarez, former head of the Small Business Administration under President Bill Clinton, is also on the board. Jami Miscik, who joined the board last year, is a former CIA deputy director of intelligence.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: The leading maker of personal computers, printers, and other tech gear, including 3D printing solutions, saw sales take off even as many other companies suffered sinking sales during the pandemic. In a year of crisis, HP reached underserved communities through $21 million in various programs, grants, and donations. These initiatives included producing more than 5 million 3D printed PPE parts to help health care workers, and printing and distributing hundreds of thousands of education booklets for young students and teachers in the U.S., Canada, India, and Haiti. Helping its workers at home meant of course providing the right technology but also not overlooking small conveniences like starting meetings five or 10 minutes after each hour to give stressed parents time to check in with their kids learning at home. “I really appreciate that so much thought and care was put into our health and well-being from the get-go,” one employee says.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: The advent of the coronavirus has played out to the benefit of the personal computer and printing giant. Although sales at HP dropped 3.6% year over year to $56.6 billion for the fiscal year ended Oct. 31, 2020, more recent quarters yielded better performance. Investors have been pleased as HP reported strong sales of PCs and printers, driven in part by the rise of remote work. As of mid-May 2021, shares had more than doubled in 12 months, to around $33. Whether the company’s computer sales will shrink as people return to the office remains to be seen.

companyRankingLists.title: Change the World
companyRankingLists.itemDescription: The personal computer and printing giant relies on plastics for many of its products—and an ever-growing share of those plastics is recycled. In 2019 HP released the Elite Dragonfly laptop and a carbon neutral–certified printer, both built using ocean-bound plastics; it also opened a recycling facility for such plastics in Haiti that will help source materials for its products. HP has also met its goal of ensuring that its branded printing paper, of which it sells thousands of tons per year, comes only from zero-deforestation sources; the company planted 1 million trees in 2020 as part of that effort.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: While HP’s sales held steady last year, its profits plunged 41%. The company's biggest highlight in recent months was its successful defense against a hostile takeover bid by copy-machine giant Xerox, initiated in the fall. Xerox executives pitched the deal as a way to create a printing powerhouse while opening up the door to cost-cutting. HP, on the other hand, claimed that the deal would be bad for investors and that the PC-and-printing giant would be better off operating alone, considering that people are buying fewer printers and computers these days. Ultimately, the coronavirus and its impact on the economy forced Xerox to call off its takeover bid.
